newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Krasnoyarsk hydro eyes international paper.
newsitem.headline: Russian Krasnoyarsk hydro eyes international paper.

text.p: Russia's Krasnoyarsk hydroelectric station is to examine the possibility of a debut on the international securities market, deputy chief executive for economics Sergey Kaminsky said on Tuesday.

He said a decision taken by shareholders last week to separate from regional power utility Krasnoyarskenergo would not mean the electric company would lose access to 75 percent of its power, which the hydroelectric station supplies.
"This is not a political step, it is a legal step," he said. "Today we are a completely independent legal entity."

He said the hydroelectric station would continue to sell to Krasnoyarskenergo but would look to sell 30-50 percent of its output on a regional electric market which he predicted could start by autumn.
Kaminsky said shareholders had authorised 100 billion roubles of new capital at the annual meeting last week. Authorised capital is currently 331.11 billion roubles.
He said they would probably make a public offering for about $10 million or 58 billion roubles, "but the board of directors will decide."
He said the board would discuss the issue at the beginning of next month.
"After shares we might launch an ADR (American Depository Receipt) issue," he added. "Or a Eurobond -- depending on which market looks more attractive."
Kaminsky said the hydro station, which did not currently have an international auditor, would carry out a tender to choose a financial consultant, probably a Moscow company.
Shareholders at the meeting approved a 1996 dividend of four roubles per ordinary share. Pre-tax profit in 1996 rose to 103.6 billion roubles from 66 billion roubles in 1995.

Krasnoyarsk hydroelectric station's main shareholders on April 1, before the shareholders' meeting, were Krasnoyarskenergo (27.9 percent), KrAZ aluminium plant (12.3 percent) and METALEKS (20 percent).
